record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Is the product space of an arbitrary family of co-sober T0 spaces again co-sober?

evidence.quote: Question 9.7. Is the product space of a family of co-sober spaces co-sober?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a $T_0$ topological space. A nonempty subset $K \subseteq X$ is called irreducible if whenever $K \subseteq A \cup B$ with $A, B$ closed in $X$, one has $K \subseteq A$ or $K \subseteq B$. Denote by $\mathrm{K}(X)$ the set of all nonempty compact saturated subsets of $X$ (a set is saturated if it equals the intersection of its open neighborhoods, equivalently if it is an upper set in the specialization order). A nonempty compact saturated subset $Q \subseteq X$ is called irreducible (in the sense of compact saturated sets) if whenever $Q \subseteq A \cup B$ with $A, B$ compact saturated, one has $Q \subseteq A$ or $Q \subseteq B$. Equivalently, $Q$ is irreducible in $\mathrm{K}(X)$ (ordered by reverse inclusion) when viewed via the upper Vietoris / Smyth structure.

The space $X$ is called co-sober if every irreducible compact saturated subset $Q$ of $X$ is of the form $\uparrow x = \{y \in X : x \leq_X y\}$ for a unique point $x \in X$, where $\leq_X$ is the specialization preorder of $X$.

Question: Is it true that for every family $\{X_i\}_{i \in I}$ of co-sober $T_0$ topological spaces, the product space $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ (with the product topology) is co-sober?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not return a definitive resolution of whether arbitrary products of co-sober $T_0$ spaces are co-sober. Related results on sobriety of products (e.g., the 2024 construction of two sober dcpo's whose product is not sober in the Scott topology) exist, but no clear answer to the co-sober product question was located. Status is therefore not verified.

status_evidence.title: Products of two sober dcpo's need not be sober
status_evidence.snippet: Two dcpo's whose Scott spaces are sober but whose order product is not sober.
status_evidence.claim: Related work shows sobriety can fail under products in dcpo settings, but does not directly resolve the co-sober product question.

status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open questions about sober and well-filtered spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The question on products of co-sober spaces is posed as an open problem in this line of research.
